subject.title: core: el cron-handler devuelve 200 en fallos parciales y oculta degradaciones operativas

question: Should the first cron-handler phase keep HTTP 200 with structured partial-failure/severity signals, or should selected routes start returning 207/5xx now?
rationale: The code change is straightforward, but the safe behavior depends on which existing partial failures are business-tolerated versus operationally alertable across shared cron apps.

options.title: Ship compatible structured signal first
options.body: Add `status`, `rejectedCount`, `rejectedReasons`, and `severity` to response/log output while keeping HTTP 200 as the default until route policies are explicit.

options.title: Define route status matrix now
options.body: Classify each critical route and implement 207/5xx behavior only for the routes where partial failures must fail operational checks immediately.

options.title: Close without handler-policy change
options.body: Keep marketplace-specific issues responsible for each symptom and leave the shared handler contract unchanged.

recommendation.title: Ship compatible structured signal first
recommendation.body: Add `status`, `rejectedCount`, `rejectedReasons`, and `severity` to response/log output while keeping HTTP 200 as the default until route policies are explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: JavierHamelyn authored the issue, is tied to the current handler snapshot by blame, and appears closest to the cross-cron policy question in the available history.
